Sudoku 9×9 on NoCharge — the fixed puzzle and its checks

What the current NoCharge Sudoku 9×9 page actually provides: one fixed 3×3-box puzzle, a number pad, row checks, and no generator or saved resume.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

The full grid, at your own pace.

Play Sudoku 9×9Browse all Articles

Bottom line: The current Sudoku 9×9 page loads a fixed nine-by-nine puzzle and bundled solution. It does not generate a fresh puzzle, offer difficulty labels, or resume a saved board after reload.

The current board and rules

Digits 1–9 must appear once in each row, column, and three-by-three box. Given cells are locked. Select an empty cell and enter a digit with the on-screen number pad; Clear cell removes the entry. The nine-by-nine page also has row and column selectors for choosing a cell.

What the Checks counter means

The engine rejects a digit that would repeat in the selected row, column, or box. If a non-repeating entry differs from the bundled solution, the page accepts it and increments the visible Checks counter. That feedback does not end the game, and it is not a difficulty rating.

Fixed content, no saved puzzle

The current source contains a fixed starting grid and its answer. It does not include a runtime generator, a uniqueness-verification pipeline, pencil marks, a Check or Reveal tool, or a saved-puzzle key. The board and Checks counter are page state; reset restores the same puzzle.

This description is deliberately narrower than older generator and difficulty claims. It does not claim that one puzzle size is better, easier, or more educational than another.
